title: Predictable Price Pressure
one_line: Days with large aggregate dividend PAYMENTS (cash reinvested by funds) earn higher market returns: +1 SD payout yield → +3.2 bp that day vs a 4.1 bp mean; above-median payment days earned 7.7%/yr vs 3.5% on other days (1926-2018), effect larger when VIX/illiquidity is high, absent in December.

findings.statement: Payout-yield coefficient 67 (t = 3.47) with year-month fixed effects; days t and t−1 only, placebo on future payments null.
Strongest in Q1; no effect in Q4/December.
Survives day-of-week, turn-of-month, FOMC and macro-announcement controls.

why.pattern: Predictable uninformed buying (dividend reinvestment) moves prices — inelastic markets.

reported_results.headline: Days with large aggregate dividend PAYMENTS (cash reinvested by funds) earn higher market returns: +1 SD payout yield → +3.2 bp that day vs a 4.1 bp mean; above-median payment days earned 7.7%/yr vs 3.5% on other days (1926-2018), effect larger when VIX/illiquidity is high, absent in December.

tradable_edge: Testable on ES only with an aggregate S&P 500 dividend PAYMENT-date calendar, which we do not have (needs per-stock pay dates). Parked: dividend_payment_day_long_es would be the spec if a free pay-date calendar is approved.
data_fit: Index-level effect, but needs S&P 500 dividend payment dates (not in Lexar data).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 5, 2026-11-10), not by the weekly pipeline.
